title: Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
summary: Reliability is a feature you engineer on purpose. SRE turns "how reliable should we be?" into a number, then spends that number to govern how fast you ship.

blocks.markdown:
SRE is operations done by software engineers, governed by explicit numbers instead of heroics.

- Treats "keep production healthy" as a **coding problem**: monitor, automate, self-heal.
- Picks a **reliability target on purpose** rather than chasing 100%.
- Settles the dev-vs-ops fight with one shared number, the **error budget**.
- Born at Google: "what happens when you ask a software engineer to design an operations team."

blocks.subTitle: Which tool for which job
blocks.markdown:
Each SRE term answers a specific question.

| Situation | Reach for |
|---|---|
| Is the service healthy? | SLI + SLO |
| Promise in a contract | SLA (money-backed) |
| Ship a risky release? | Error budget |
| Repetitive manual ops | Automate the toil |
| Just had an outage | Blameless postmortem |

blocks.subTitle: SLI, SLO, SLA
blocks.markdown:
Three terms stack from raw signal to legal promise.

- **SLI** is a *measurement* of one quality aspect, usually good events ÷ total events (e.g. % of requests that succeed).
- **SLO** is the internal *target* for an SLI over a window, e.g. 99.9% over rolling 28 days.
- **SLA** is an external *contract* with consequences (refunds) for missing it.
- Measure SLIs from the **user's vantage point**, and keep the SLA **looser than the SLO** for margin.

blocks.subTitle: What the nines cost
blocks.markdown:
Every extra nine cuts allowed downtime by 10×, so high nines get brutally expensive.

| SLO | Downtime / year |
|---|---|
| 99% | ~3.65 days |
| 99.9% | ~8.8 hours |
| 99.99% | ~53 minutes |
| 99.999% | ~5 minutes |

Five nines leaves almost no room for a human to even react, so it must be fully automated.

blocks.subTitle: Error budget
blocks.markdown:
The error budget is simply **100% − SLO** — the unreliability you are explicitly allowed.

![Error budget gating releases](assets/e07-site-reliability-engineering/error-budget-gates-releases.svg)

- A 99.9% SLO gives a 0.1% budget — about **40 minutes** of allowed badness over 28 days.
- Treat it as a **resource to spend** on risky deploys, experiments, maintenance.
- Budget left → ship freely. Budget exhausted → freeze releases and fix reliability.
- The **number decides**, not an argument.

blocks.subTitle: The feedback loop
blocks.markdown:
Day-to-day SRE is a closed loop that should get quieter each pass.

![SRE feedback loop](assets/e07-site-reliability-engineering/sre-feedback-loop.svg)

- **Monitor** continuously, **alert** a human only when action is needed.
- On-call **responds**, then writes a blameless **postmortem**.
- Lessons feed back as **improvements** — better monitoring, automation, fixes.
- Each loop should reduce how often you need the next one.

blocks.subTitle: Golden signals & burn rate
blocks.markdown:
Page a human only when a human must act right now — everything else is a ticket or dashboard.

- Google's **four golden signals**: **latency**, **traffic**, **errors**, **saturation** (the resource closest to its limit).
- Alert on **symptoms users feel**, not every internal cause, to avoid alert fatigue.
- Modern pattern: alert on **error-budget burn rate**. 1× uses the whole window's budget exactly; 14.4× burns a 30-day budget in ~2 hours — page now.
- One rule pages fast on severe issues, quietly on minor ones.

blocks.subTitle: Toil & automation
blocks.markdown:
Toil is the operational work you automate away instead of suffering.

![Reducing toil through automation](assets/e07-site-reliability-engineering/reducing-toil.svg)

- **Toil** = work that is manual, repetitive, automatable, reactive, and scales linearly with the service.
- It crowds out engineering, burns people out, and grows with traffic.
- Google caps SRE toil at **≤50% of time**, freeing the rest for automation that removes future toil.
- Every manual fix is a prompt: "can the machine do this next time?"

blocks.subTitle: The knobs you turn
blocks.markdown:
Every SRE decision trades reliability against something else.

- **Reliability vs velocity** — the error budget converts this into a shared number.
- **Cost vs nines** — each nine multiplies cost; buy only up to where users notice.
- **Alert sensitivity vs fatigue** — tune toward "every page is actionable."
- **Manual control vs automation** — automation removes toil but can fail fast and at scale.
- A **too-tight SLO** paradoxically slows shipping, since every launch threatens the tiny budget.

blocks.subTitle: Decision rules
blocks.markdown:
Plain rules for setting targets and alerts.

- If users **can't perceive** the extra nine, don't buy it.
- If the budget is **healthy**, let devs ship — that's what it's for.
- If the budget is **blown**, freeze launches and do reliability work, automatically.
- If an alert wouldn't make you act right now, it's **not a page**.
- If a task is manual, repetitive, and recurring, **automate it** — unless automation costs more than the toil it removes.

blocks.subTitle: Real systems
blocks.markdown:
The big players each lean on a different half of SRE.

- **Google** invented it: SREs cap toil at 50% and refuse work past it, forcing automation. Error budgets end the dev-vs-ops standoff.
- **Amazon/AWS** — "you build it, you run it"; public SLAs with credits, plus blameless **Correction of Errors** docs.
- **Netflix** — **Chaos Engineering** (Chaos Monkey) kills prod instances on purpose to prove resilience.
- **Stripe / payments** run *tighter* SLOs because a failed payment costs revenue and trust directly.

blocks.subTitle: What to watch
blocks.markdown:
A handful of signals tell you whether reliability is on track.

- **Error budget remaining** — the headline; hitting zero triggers the freeze policy.
- **Burn rate** — a sudden high burn (>10×) means an active severe incident, page now.
- **The four golden signals** — latency, traffic, errors, saturation.
- **Toil %** — trending above ~50% means automation is losing the race.
- **Page volume & actionability**, plus **MTTD / MTTA / MTTR** to see where response is degrading.

The misconceptions that trip people up:

- **"SRE is just renamed ops."** No — reliability is solved with software and governed by SLOs and budgets; 100% toil means doing it wrong.
- **"Higher reliability is always better."** Past what users perceive, extra nines cost a fortune and starve your budget.
- **"The error budget is a punishment."** It's *permission* to take risks until you've spent it.
- **"Blameless means no accountability."** No personal blame, but the team owns tracked action items.
- **"SLA and SLO are the same."** SLO is internal aspiration; SLA is a looser external promise with money attached.
